title: Waterloo docstring structure
summary: Profiles, sections, subsections, and scope rules.

items: A source object must be at least as public as its target object.
Public_* sections describe contained objects that must not be more public than the container.
Derived_from and Contract.base follow the same monotonicity rule as See_also.
Waterloo indentation uses only TAB and SPC4 (four spaces).
Some waterlint commands name these modes tab and spc4.
Follow the indentation style already used in the surrounding document.
Keep indentation consistent within one docstring.
Do not mix tabs and spaces in the same structural block.
Indentation expresses hierarchy, not just visual layout.
Use Preamble to declare profile and normative sections.
Derive the section and subsection inventory from SECTION_PROPERTIES.
Keep the section list consistent with the object kind and profile.
Use subsections only where SECTION_PROPERTIES defines them.
Use waterlint explain-section to inspect sections and waterlint explain-subsection to inspect subsections.
Keep scope monotonicity between source and target objects.
